language.script_notes: Some Aymara/Andean Indigenous cultural presence near the Bolivian/Peruvian border.
false_friends: Southern Peru (shares the same Atacama-adjacent coastal desert)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Often minimal on remote desert highways.
road_furniture.line_paint: Long, straight desert roads with wide shoulders.
road_furniture.curb_style: Minimal to absent outside towns; vast stretches of unmarked open desert.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Mining company signage common given the region's copper mining industry.

architecture.roof_style: Flat or very low-pitch roofs, suited to the near-total absence of rain.
architecture.roof_material: Simple corrugated metal or flat construction, reflecting minimal weather protection needs.
architecture.wall_construction: Utilitarian mining-town construction dominates; colourful port-city architecture in Iquique and Antofagasta; adobe/Andean-influenced construction near the Bolivian border (San Pedro de Atacama).
architecture.wall_color_palette: Dusty, sun-bleached tones matching the surrounding desert; some brightly painted port-city buildings.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Large-scale copper mining infrastructure; sparse desert towns; adobe Andean-style architecture near San Pedro de Atacama; nitrate ghost towns (Humberstone) as unique regional landmarks.

nature.vegetation: Almost entirely devoid of vegetation across the hyper-arid Atacama core — among the driest, most vegetation-free landscapes on Earth; sparse cacti and hardy shrubs appear only at higher altitude near the Andes.
nature.terrain: The Atacama Desert, the driest non-polar desert on Earth (some areas have never recorded rainfall), dominates the region; salt flats, geysers and volcanic peaks appear at higher elevation near the Bolivian border.
nature.climate_signature: Stark, barren, reddish-brown desert terrain with almost no vegetation — one of the most visually distinctive, empty landscapes anywhere, unmistakable once recognized.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Heavy mining trucks and 4WD vehicles common given the region's copper mining industry and rugged desert terrain.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Coverage concentrated along the Pan-American Highway and mining towns.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Sparse outside the main highway and towns, with vast uncovered desert stretches in between.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shares the same Atacama-adjacent coastal desert stretching across the border, similarly barren terrain
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Chilean plates and yellow-reflector bollards differ from Peru's road furniture; Peru's coastal desert cities generally show more visible Andean cultural influence and different architecture.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Norte Grande is stark, barren desert with almost no vegetation; Central Chile is green farmland and vineyards, and southern Chile is lush temperate rainforest and glaciers — both look nothing like the Atacama.
